name: Aruamu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only Z'graggen 1971 comparative material and subclassification notes; Wikipedia stub has no phonology; no stress-covering description found.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1951. Languages of Bogia District, New Guinea [part 1]. Oceania 22(2): 130-147. doi:10.1002/j.1834-4461.1951.tb00554.x. Sec. 5 'Makarub', pp. 138-141.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Makarub section gives a phoneme chart ('Sound system'), notes on devoiced plosives and vowels, nominal endings, pronouns, verb tenses and a text, but NO sentence about stress. Forms are stress-marked (ku'masim(u) 'man', 'kwarim(u) 'ear', aru'am(u) 'big', wa'tepem(u) 'short', ko'wap(u), mu'ket). The only stress prose in the article concerns Watam (p.132, 'a tendency to final stress may be observed', from Poech's list) and Murusapa (p.144, 'Stress tends to be antepenultimate').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid arua1260 (and Glottolog 5.1 CLDF sources.bib entries tagged [msy]).
sources.note: No grammar, sketch or phonology reference; only Poech 1908, Schebesta 1913/1921-22, Ray 1919, Capell 1951-52/1962, Z'graggen 1969/1971/1972/1974, Foley 2005, and a 1998 Bible-story booklet.

sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Aruamu language [msy], up-to-date as of 2025-11-04 (the Internet Archive 2026-01-04 of language-archives.org/language/msy).
sources.note: Lists only Crubadan, Rosetta Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, WALS, Ethnologue, and PARADISEC audio (Daniels 2010 DD1-034/035; Daniels 2024 DD1-1088/1166; Barth 2022 DGB1-msy01-03). No language description.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2023. A grammar of Ulwa (Papua New Guinea). Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Mikarew/Aruamu listed among Ramu languages only; no Aruamu data.

sources.note: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available'; the bibliography of published and unpublished works has no Aruamu entry (index runs Arop-Sissano, Asaro'o). No OPD or phonology MS catalogued.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In Pawley et al. (eds.), Papuan Pasts (PL 572), 109-144.
sources.note: Mikarew appears only in comparative pronoun/lexical tables; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: transnewguinea.org, language page 'Aruamu' (64 items from Foley 2005).
sources.note: Forms not stress-marked; no phonology notes.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/146580.
sources.note: Explicitly silent: printed p.6 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Sec. 2.23.12 Misegian Family (Mikarew 52, Sepen, Giri) pp.77-78 and Ruboni Stock features pp.78-79 are segmental only ('None of the languages appears to be tonal'); sec. 3.56.1 Mikarew verb structure, no prosody. Notes that Capell (1952:138ff) 'under the name Makarup, gives a phoneme chart, notes on grammar, a text and a wordlist' and that Fr. Schorr SVD compiled an unpublished dictionary.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1952. Languages of Bogia District, New Guinea [part 2]. Oceania 22(3): 178-207 (comparative vocabulary with a Makarub column, pp. 198ff).
sources.note: Stress-marked Makarub vocabulary only (ku'masimu man, a'misimu woman, a'pistemu father, a'mebamu mother, ta'panimu head, 'narisimu hair, ta'masimu eye, 'winibamu nose, aka'torimu mouth, 'kwarimu ear); no prose statement.

sources.citation: Aruamu Dictionary (Aruamu - English - Tok Pisin). Webonary.org, SIL International, n.d. [online dictionary of the Aruamu dictionary project, Pioneer Bible Translators; project led by Marsha Relyea Miles per PBT/news records].https://www.webonary.org/aruamu/
Relyea, Marsha. 1992a. A comparative grammar of Aruamu and Kire. Unpublished manuscript, Pioneer Bible Translators, Madang, Papua New Guinea.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only substantial grammatical description of Aruamu known (cited by Foley 2024 for Aruamu morphology); a PBT translator's grammar of this kind normally opens with a phonology section including stress. Not catalogued by SIL-PNG, OLAC or Glottolog; would have to be requested from PBT (Madang/Dallas) or from Foley.
